macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street rebounds in technology-led rally
items.summary: The Nasdaq Composite jumped 6.51%, the S&P 500 gained 4.73%, and the Dow rose 3.01% in the strongest U.S. session since April 2025, according to market reports.[2][6]

items.title: Nvidia shares surge after Jensen Huang reinstated as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia rose about 31–33% after its board restored Jensen Huang as chief executive, adding roughly $900 billion to $950 billion in market value and lifting semiconductor and AI-related stocks.[1][7]

items.title: U.S. stock futures turn lower after rally
items.summary: U.S. futures declined as investors reassessed Monday’s sharp gains: Nasdaq 100 futures were down about 1.7%, S&P 500 futures 0.8%, and Dow futures 0.4% in premarket trading.[4][8]

items.title: Fed officials signal further action may be needed on inflation
items.summary: New York Fed President John Williams said monetary policymakers need to act in a timely and sustained way to return inflation to the 2% target, while markets continued to price a likely December rate increase.[2][4]

items.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise raises outlook and announces buyback
items.summary: HPE reported fiscal fourth-quarter revenue of $14.55 billion and free cash flow of $1.92 billion, both above expectations, and announced an additional $5 billion share-repurchase authorization. Its shares nevertheless fell about 11% before the open.[2][4]

items.title: Investors await major technology earnings
items.summary: Dell Technologies, Autodesk, Workday, HP and Urban Outfitters were scheduled to report earnings after the U.S. market close, with Analog Devices and other companies reporting before the open.[4][8]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: CFTC permits regulated exchanges to count crypto toward reserves
items.summary: The U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission said regulated derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses may include Bitcoin, Ether and certain stablecoins in financial reserves, subject to valuation haircuts and risk controls.[3]

items.title: South Korea proposes digital-asset framework and ICO return
items.summary: South Korea’s draft digital-asset legislation would create a comprehensive regulatory framework, permit domestic initial coin offerings under conditions and cap exchange shareholder ownership at 20%; the proposal also favors bank-led stablecoin issuance.[1][4]

items.title: Crypto market remains broadly lower
items.summary: Market coverage reported a weak session, with Bitcoin rebounding toward $61,000 while many major altcoins declined; GRT, XRP and SNX were among notable daily losers, falling roughly 9%.[2][3]

items.title: Ethereum Foundation expands security effort and plans quantum-resistant migration
items.summary: The Ethereum Foundation reportedly plans to complete a quantum-resistant cryptography migration by 2029 and has expanded its protocol-security team ahead of the overhaul.[4][5]

items.title: BitMine increases Ethereum treasury
items.summary: BitMine added 7,819 ETH over the past week, bringing reported holdings to approximately 6.086 million ETH, or 4.98% of total Ether supply.[8]

items.title: Swiss institutions test tokenized settlement
items.summary: The Swiss National Bank, UBS and SIX are exploring a shared-ledger pilot for tokenized securities and money settlement under Project Helvetia.[2][3]

items.title: Hyperliquid records new daily priority-fee high
items.summary: Hyperliquid’s on-chain priority-fee revenue reportedly reached $664,500 in one day, about 20% above its previous record.[4]

items.title: Arkham launches government crypto holdings tracker
items.summary: Blockchain intelligence firm Arkham launched a dashboard tracking government-controlled on-chain assets, with reported holdings totaling about $23.79 billion.[2]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.4 loop-transformer model
items.summary: Z.ai released GLM-5.4, a 750-billion-parameter model using a loop-transformer architecture that repeatedly processes some layers to improve reasoning and coding performance.[1][2]

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Ship for software teams
items.summary: Anthropic introduced Claude Ship, an agentic developer tool that reviews GitHub pull requests, fixes bugs, and can approve changes under organization-defined rules.[1][3]

items.title: Google DeepMind reports AI-designed quantum algorithms
items.summary: Google DeepMind researchers used teams of AI agents and formal verification to discover faster quantum algorithms relevant to fusion energy and chemistry.[2]

items.title: Nvidia releases open diffusion language models
items.summary: Nvidia released Nemotron-Labs-Sigma, a collection of 14 open diffusion language models in 3B and 8B sizes, reporting average generation speedups of about 3.46 times.[1]

items.title: Researchers introduce BioEmu2 for biomolecular simulation
items.summary: BioEmu2 uses generative modeling to emulate atomically resolved dynamics of proteins, nucleic acids, ligands, and ions at speeds far beyond conventional molecular-dynamics simulations.[2]

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco announce open-source Linux security runtime
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco launched Shirudo, an open-source agent-based runtime designed to protect Linux systems from exploits while security patches are being deployed.[3]

items.title: OpenAI reports higher autonomous research-task completion
items.summary: OpenAI reported that its agents now complete 46% of research tasks estimated to require two to four hours of human work, up from 23% in March.[9]

items.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini
items.summary: Thinking Machines Lab released Inkling 2 Mini, a 26.4-billion-parameter open-weights model with 3.4 billion active parameters designed for local laptop use.[8]

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: GTA VI reported as PlayStation’s biggest launch
items.summary: Sony says Grand Theft Auto VI became the biggest launch in PlayStation history, with more than 39 million PS5 owners reportedly playing it during its first four days. The game also received its first patch.

items.title: Ubisoft creates generative-AI game studio
items.summary: Ubisoft has reportedly founded Motherbrain, a studio focused on using generative artificial intelligence in game development.

items.title: Plug In Digital acquires Twin Sails Interactive
items.summary: Plug In Digital announced the acquisition of independent publisher Twin Sails Interactive and plans to combine the businesses into a larger publishing and distribution group.

items.title: Tiny Bookshop surpasses one million sales
items.summary: Skystone and neoludic announced that Tiny Bookshop has sold one million copies. Its Arts & Crafts DLC is scheduled for release on December 5, 2026.

items.title: Dawn of War IV launch date confirmed
items.summary: Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War IV is scheduled to launch on December 3, 2026, while the Commander Edition will provide three days of early access.

items.title: League of Legends announces New Dawn update
items.summary: Riot Games revealed another League of Legends rework, titled New Dawn, during the Worlds 2026 final.

items.title: Deltarune Chapter 6 reaches structural completion
items.summary: Toby Fox said Deltarune Chapter 6 is structurally complete and that development on Chapter 7 has begun.

items.title: Firaxis reportedly announces layoffs
items.summary: Firaxis was reported to have carried out layoffs amid broader difficulties across the video game industry.

items.title: Team Liquid and Friendly Fire plan gaming café network
items.summary: Team Liquid and Friendly Fire announced a partnership to create a network of esports and gaming cafés in local communities.

items.title: AION 2 Season 2 dated
items.summary: AION 2’s second season, titled Season 2, is scheduled to begin on December 16, 2026.

tech_news.query: What are the most important technology news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major product launches, company news, and significant tech industry developments. Exclude AI-specific news.

items.title: CrowdStrike to acquire Zscaler for $43.9 billion
items.summary: CrowdStrike agreed to acquire Zscaler in an all-stock transaction valued at approximately $43.9 billion, which would become the largest cybersecurity acquisition on record. The deal combines two major cybersecurity companies amid rising cyber threats.[1][6]

items.title: Uber, Lucid and Nuro begin driverless robotaxi testing
items.summary: Uber, Lucid and Nuro reportedly began fully driverless robotaxi testing on public roads in the San Francisco Bay Area, ahead of a planned public launch in the first quarter of 2027.[1]

items.title: Kagi launches paid email service
items.summary: Search company Kagi launched Kagi Mail, a paid email service positioned as an alternative to Gmail.[1]

items.title: Huawei Mate 90 Air launch and specifications reported
items.summary: Huawei is expected to unveil the Mate 90 Air on November 24, with reported memory configurations and color options revealed ahead of the launch.[1]
